Abstract:

The study of finite geometries associated with Hermitian varieties offers a rich framework for examining the relationship between incidence structures, polar spaces, and finite classical geometries. This thesis deals with the characterization of secant lines and non-singular hyperplanes of Hermitian varieties in projective spaces over finite fields. First we consider the characterization of secant lines in PG(3, q2) and then in PG(4, q2). In such circumstances we impose appropriate incidence conditions on a collection of lines and study the obtained point-line incidence structures by looking at the interaction of points, pencils and planes in dimension 3, and points, planes and solids in dimension 4.
These structures lead to generalized quadrangles from which the underlying Hermitian variety and its secant lines are reconstructed. As a consequence, the geometric and incidence features of the line set are demonstrated to characterize the secants of a non-singular Hermitian variety. A generalization to PG(s, q2) is also considered, where required conditions are shown and a partial converse is proved, leading to a quasi-Hermitian point set. The thesis also deals with non-singular hyperplanes of Hermitian varieties and their incidence features. The results are of importance for the understanding of the interaction between local incidence conditions and global geometric structures in finite projective spaces.

Keywords: Characterization problems, Generalized quadrangles, Hermitian forms, Non-singular Hermitianvarieties, Non-singular hyperplanes, Projective spaces, Quasi-Hermitian varieties, Secant lines.
